task_graph.objective: Resolve sign-in method for the WARDEN mobile app, since it becomes the identity RevenueCat ties subscriptions to.
task_graph.deliverable: Decision: Sign in with Apple (iOS) + Sign in with Google (Android), no email/password path in v1.
task_graph.success_criteria: Zero-friction signup with no email-sending infrastructure to build/maintain. Satisfies Apple App Store policy (any third-party social login on iOS requires offering Sign in with Apple, so building Apple+Google directly avoids a later forced add). Standard pattern for subscription-conversion mobile apps — fewer signup dropoffs between 'see your exposure' and 'start free trial'. Trade-off accepted: one-time OAuth config per platform vs. magic-link email plumbing or password-reset ownership.

task_graph.objective: Decide how the on-device model for exposure summarization is implemented, given it was scoped as low-stakes/optional (not safety-critical).
task_graph.deliverable: Decision: use platform-native on-device APIs where available (iOS Foundation Models framework, Android Gemini Nano via AICore) with a plain template-string fallback (no model) everywhere else. Do not bundle a cross-platform LLM (e.g. GGUF via llama.cpp/MLX).
task_graph.success_criteria: Matches the earlier ML-strategy finding that this feature is optional and not privacy/latency-critical (broker listings are public data) — a bundled model would add app size and eval burden disproportionate to the feature's value. Template fallback means the feature always works, just with less natural phrasing on older/non-flagship devices.

task_graph.objective: Decide the subscription/paywall structure for RevenueCat given the locked MVP scope (free scan + paid continuous monitoring only; no auto-removal or family plan in v1).
task_graph.deliverable: Decision: single entitlement ('Monitoring') with monthly and annual package options. Free tier = one-time scan, no re-scan. No additional entitlements/tiers in v1.
task_graph.success_criteria: Minimizes RevenueCat dashboard configuration and paywall UI complexity to match the already-locked single-tier MVP; family plan and auto-removal entitlements can be added later without restructuring the existing one.

task_graph.objective: Decide where the mobile app's code lives relative to the existing CORTEGE repo.
task_graph.deliverable: Decision: add a top-level mobile/ Expo project inside the existing cortege-hackathon repo (single repo, single deploy target for the shared server). No separate repo, no monorepo tooling (Turborepo/Nx).
task_graph.success_criteria: Consistent with the already-locked decision to extend the existing server rather than extract it. There's minimal code to share between the Vite/React web app and the Expo/RN app (at most types/constants), so multi-repo or workspace tooling overhead isn't justified.
